$comment: SQL / KQL LITERAL DIALECT SITES — consumed by scripts/ci/check-sql-literal-dialect.mjs.
Each entry is a console source file that builds string literals for an engine whose
literal grammar is NOT T-SQL quote doubling: Spark / Databricks SQL and KQL regular
escapeKqlLiteral). `tsqlEscapeAllowance` is the EXACT number of T-SQL-rule escapes
or escapeLiteralFor(...)) the file may contain, and `reason` names the engine each one
feeds. The count is exact in both directions: a higher count is a new doubling site in
a Spark/KQL file; a lower count is a stale allowance that must be lowered so the
headroom cannot absorb a later regression.
engine: spark | kql | mixed (the file builds statements for more than one engine).
tsqlClientFiles: files that IMPORT a Databricks or Kusto statement client
(databricks-client, kusto-client, monitor-client) and also hold T-SQL-rule escapes
that feed a quote-doubling grammar (T-SQL, OData, DAX, Postgres, KQL verbatim @'...').
`tsqlEscapes` is the EXACT count, and `reason` names the engine those escapes feed. An
importer that is in neither list may hold no T-SQL-rule escape at all.
